evidence.appropriate: the name's own C and L, set in the book serif and double-underlined like a total: the ledger's sign on the ledger's initials
evidence.distinctive: nobody in the five uses a serif monogram or a rule; but CL serif monograms are a stock-library staple, so the double rule carries the difference
evidence.simple: two letters and two rules, 55 anchors; drawable from memory
evidence.legible: CL reads at 16 px with the favicon's emboldened letters and one thick rule (thinnest 1.41 px); the wordmark passes at 120 px at cap 450
evidence.adaptable: works in one colour and reversed; favicon redrawn heavier with wider spacing; letters as the icon from day one
evidence.timeless: a book serif monogram is the Sage's register, not a trend; no avoid item
evidence.universal: mirrored reads as a backwards JC only as a mirror should; rotated shows letters on their side, no second reading
evidence.clear: description search found stock CL serif monograms in quantity (Shutterstock, Adobe Stock), none with a double rule; the full knock-out comes in refinement
evidence.congruent: book serif in title case, level rules, symmetric balance, medium weight and open counters match the targets and the light front-vowel name
evidence.system: symbol and wordmark share Newsreader; every lockup and tier builds; rationale draft in critique.md
